answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 39% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the horizon calculation reruns each epoch, the garden weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the river settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 68 clones hence holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 19 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
